title: Representative chat streaming workload generator (v1): concurrency + prompt-length dist + streaming cadence, validated vs prod telemetry
creator: Jonas Weber
content:
## Context
We need a representative *chat streaming* workload for the Q1 2026 perf baseline and ongoing regression gating. The workload must mirror production traffic shapes (prompt size distribution, output size distribution, concurrency patterns, and streaming cadence) without using sensitive prompt content.

This ticket covers defining and implementing the workload generator and validating it against production telemetry cohorts (per ADR-0173). It is intended to be used by the benchmark harness and perf-canary.

## Goals
- Implement a deterministic chat streaming workload generator usable in CI and on benchmark fleets.
- Realistic concurrency + ramp: support steady-state and burst patterns seen in prod.
- Prompt-length distribution and decode-length distribution approximating production cohorts.
- Streaming cadence that matches server push behavior while preventing client-side read bottlenecks from contaminating TTFT/TPOT.
- Output metrics and tags aligned with ADR-0172 (TTFT/TPOT/throughput) and include enough run metadata to attribute regressions.

## Non-goals
- Perfect replication of every customer traffic pattern (v1 is "top cohorts" only).
- Customer prompt content (we use synthetic prompts / templated content only).
- Full tool/function calling multi-turn behavior (separate workload workstream).

## Definitions / measurement boundaries
- TTFT (streaming): time from request accepted by server to first token written to response stream ("first token on wire"), excluding client-side buffering.
- TPOT (streaming): average time per output token *on the server*, computed as (t_last_token - t_first_token) / (n_output_tokens - 1). Also export client-observed TPOT for debugging, but gating uses server-side.
- Throughput: tokens/sec at server aggregated across workers; for streaming runs also export active_streams over time.

Implementation must record both server-side and client-side timings and include a guardrail that flags likely client bottlenecks (e.g., when client read loop falls behind and stream buffer grows).

## Workload spec (v1)
### Request shape
- Endpoint/mode: Chat Completions, streaming=true
- Synthetic messages:
  - system: short fixed instruction
  - user: templated text with parameterized token length
  - optional: 1 prior assistant turn to reflect common "multi-turn" without tool calling
- Sampling:
  - prompt token length bins derived from prod histograms (telemetry cohort: "chat_streaming_default")
  - output tokens: sampled from a capped log-normal distribution (to reflect long-tail), with per-bin caps to prevent runaway variance in CI
- Determinism:
  - workload_seed controls request ordering and per-request parameter draws
  - fixed RNG algorithm and versioned config

### Concurrency + arrival model
- Concurrency target C is configurable; generator supports:
  1) steady state: maintain C active streams (closed-loop)
  2) burst: ramp to C over R seconds, hold, then ramp down
- Default baseline profile (used in baseline sweeps unless overridden by manifest):
  - warmup: 2 minutes (discarded)
  - measure: 10 minutes
  - closed-loop target concurrency: 32 (also run 8 and 64 as coverage points in nightly)
  - burst variant: ramp 0→32 over 60s, hold 240s, ramp 32→0 over 60s

### Streaming cadence
- Client reads as fast as possible but without causing artificial backpressure:
  - use async streaming reader with bounded per-iteration work
  - explicitly disable pretty-print / logging per token
- To avoid measuring client overhead as TPOT:
  - server emits periodic "stream progress" timestamps in debug headers for sampled requests (1% sampling) to compare client-observed vs server-observed deltas
  - harness exports "client_lag_ms_p95" and fails the run if above threshold (default: 15ms) unless allow_client_lag=true

## Validation vs production telemetry
Validation steps required prior to closing this ticket:
1) Compare generated prompt length distribution (tokens) to telemetry histogram:
   - match p50/p90/p95 within +/-10% and KL divergence below threshold (see methodology notes)
2) Compare output length distribution:
   - match p50/p90/p95 within +/-15% (output length varies more, acceptable wider band)
3) Concurrency patterns:
   - confirm active_streams time series resembles production diurnal burstiness on a normalized scale (qualitative OK for v1)
4) Streaming cadence sanity:
   - ensure TTFT is not correlated with client machine load in controlled test (run generator on underpowered client; server-side TTFT should remain stable)

## Acceptance criteria
- Generator implemented in benchmark-lab with:
  - config file defining bins/weights + default profiles
  - deterministic seeding and reproducible run manifest integration
  - outputs: per-run summary + per-request sample (sampled) + aggregated percentiles
- Metrics exported:
  - TTFT p50/p95/p99 (server + client)
  - TPOT p50/p95/p99 (server + client)
  - active_streams, queue_wait_ms (if available), tokens/sec
  - client_lag_ms
- Docs: README section explaining how to run, common pitfalls (client bottleneck, warmup), and how to validate against telemetry snapshot.
- Validation report attached in this ticket (link + short summary in update).

## Implementation notes
- Config versioning: chat_streaming_v1.yaml is versioned and referenced in the run manifest as workload_version.
- Telemetry snapshot: use aggregated histograms exported by Logan Wright’s pipeline; do not copy raw prompts.
- Run naming convention:
  - workload=chat_streaming
  - scenario=cold|warm (warm uses prefix/KV cache enabled; report both)
  - concurrency=C
  - region + sku included via harness

## Links
- PR (workload generator): sources/github/benchmark-lab/pr-21455-implement-chat-streaming-workload-generator.json
- Manifest schema dependency: sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4822-benchmark-harness-run-manifest-and-results-schema.json
- Methodology/metrics ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0172-benchmark-metrics-and-run-manifest-format.json
- Workload sourcing ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0173-representative-workload-sourcing-from-prod-telemetry.json
- Slack metric boundary debate: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1763261084.json
- Slack streaming pacing discussion: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1763935150.json

## Results summary (validation)
- Prompt length distribution vs telemetry (chat_streaming_default cohort):
  - p50: within 6%
  - p90: within 8%
  - p95: within 9%
  - KL divergence: below threshold (see linked validation doc in PR)
- Output length distribution:
  - p50 within 10%, p90 within 12%, p95 within 14%
- Client overhead guardrail:
  - On standard bench client, client_lag_ms_p95 < 5ms across runs
  - On stressed client test, server-side TTFT/TPOT stable; client-side TPOT worsened and guardrail triggered as expected

## Follow-ups / TODOs
- Add optional multi-turn template (2–4 turns) to better reflect agentic chat without tool calling (candidate for workload suite v2).
- Once scheduler queueing instrumentation (ENG-4826) is available, include queue_wait_ms in exported summary and add correlation plot in dashboards.
- Consider adding a server-side "first-token-ready" metric (pre-network) if we need tighter isolation of transport effects.
